notes:
Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Team: 3 PMs + 5 Engs owning AI features. Currently on competitor (OpenAI) for chat+embeddings; evaluating Redwood Hosted as drop-in and path to Dedicated. Key asks: 1) compat layer for existing OpenAI calls (minimal client churn), 2) prompt parity with existing system, 3) measurable regression detection for LLM outputs, 4) pricing that doesn't spike token costs after migration.

Summary of recent: hosted POC ran Feb-Mar. We onboarded a subset of prod prompts and ran side-by-side comparison (OpenAI vs Redwood-hosted gpt-like open model). Found several prompt-parity regressions in multi-turn support flows (shorter clarifications, more hallucinations on rare KB facts). Redwood SE (Maya) suggested prompt tuning + quantization profile to match latency/cost. They delivered a patch for prompt templates and a model variant with tightened temperature. Client quote on 2025-03-03 demo: "Response style is close but we need exactness on policy text — even small hallucinations break legal workflow."

Security: require SSO (Okta), enterprise audit logs, KMS for encryption at rest; plan to start with Hosted (data isolation via token-level controls) then migrate to Dedicated with VPC peering, HSM for key control. Procurement wants committed monthly baseline for Dedicated (targeting 150M tokens/month).

Commercial: asked for committed-GPU pricing vs hosted per-token. Finance wants a 12–18 month blended ARR commitment, plus a clause for model regression credits if quality drops post-migration. Red flags: need an explicit SLA for latency on Dedicated and a rollback path to Hosted if canary shows degradation.

AE notes: client is pragmatic, cares about engineering effort. Expect procurement to push for migration discount and an integration window.

Stated priorities (customer): prompt parity > latency > cost (in that order).
